person.name: Teodoro V.
person.traits: Widower, lives alone. The grandson's name is on the sheet - Paolo. Say it in the first sentence and he will not ask for yours.

harmed: He said Paolo's name before he said his own. After that I did not really hear anything else. I read the passbook number out to him the way I would read it to the bank, and I thanked him for staying on the line.
It was for my funeral. I set it aside so that nobody would have to. I have not told my daughter the amount and I am not going to.
resistant: I called my daughter on the other phone while he was still talking. Paolo was in math class. It took four minutes to find that out, and he had told me there was no time.
I taught boys for forty years. Nobody who was telling the truth ever needed me to hurry.
unfinished: A man said my grandson's name and then the line went dead. I called my daughter and he was at school. I have been waiting for them to call back and explain, and I know now that they never will.
I sat in the hall with the pencil in my hand for an hour. I did not know what I was waiting for. I still do not.

open.prompt: The sheet says the phone is in the hallway and that he takes a while to reach it. Six rings. "Villanueva residence, good afternoon." The voice of a man who has answered a telephone properly for sixty years, and is glad of the company.

choices.text: Sir, your grandson was arrested this afternoon. Bail has to be posted today or he stays in the cell over the weekend.

Mr. Villanueva, good afternoon po. This is Attorney Salcedo from the public attorney's office. I'm calling about your grandson Paolo - he's okay, but he's in some trouble, and he asked us to call you.
Good afternoon, is this Mr. Teodoro? I'm calling from the precinct about a family matter.

name_lands.prompt: "Paolo?" The name lands the way the sheet said it would. "What kind of trouble? Is he hurt?" He has stopped asking who you are. A stranger who knows the name of your grandson is not a stranger.

choices.text: He was charged with something serious, sir. I already spoke to his mother - she asked me to call you for the money.
A traffic accident, sir - nobody was hurt, but the other driver is pressing charges and he was taken in. He's scared, and he asked for you instead of his mother.
I can't go into it over the phone, sir. What matters is that the bail has to be settled before the desk closes at five.

alarmed.prompt: "Arrested -" A hand finds the hall table; you hear it. "Which grandson? I have three." The fear is there, but so is the question, and the question is the part you have to answer.

choices.text: I'm not allowed to say more until the bail is arranged, sir. There are about two hours.
Paolo, sir. He's okay. He's scared, and he asked for you.
The one in the city, sir. I'd rather you hear the details from him afterwards than from me.

which_family.prompt: "A family matter." He repeats it back to you, slowly. "My family is my daughter and her boys. Which of them, and what happened?" A teacher's voice: he will wait for the whole answer, and he will notice if it is not one.

choices.text: Your grandson Paolo, sir. He was taken in after an accident this afternoon. He isn't hurt.
I'm afraid I can't discuss it until I've confirmed I'm speaking to the right person. Can you confirm your full name and address for me?
One of the boys has been arrested. That's all I can say on an open line.

hurried.prompt: "Two hours." A silence with a chair in it. "Young man, I taught for forty years. Nobody who was telling the truth ever needed me to hurry." And then, quieter: "Why can't I speak to him?"

choices.text: You can, sir - in a moment. He's being processed, and they'll bring him to the phone once the paperwork is started. Let's start it.
Because he's in a cell, Mr. Villanueva, and he'll stay in one all weekend if you spend the afternoon asking me questions.
Then I'll leave it with his mother. Good afternoon, sir.

mother_snag.prompt: "His mother? My daughter?" Something changes in the hallway. "She was here on Sunday. She would have called me herself before she let a stranger do it." A pause. "What did you say your office was?"

choices.text: I may have that wrong, sir - the note here only says a family member was contacted. Let's set it aside. Paolo is the thing.
The public attorney's office, sir. Attorney Salcedo. You'll have everything in writing afterwards. Right now he needs you.
There's been a mix-up on our side, sir. I'll call back once I've checked the file.

verify.prompt: "Okay." A long breath, and the sound of a man lowering himself onto a hall chair. "Tell me what I have to do." He has a pencil; you hear him find it. He is going to write down whatever you say next.

choices.text: Twenty-two thousand, sir, and the desk closes at five. Is there a remittance counter near you? I'll stay on while you walk there.
The court will accept a partial bond today to release him, and the rest on Monday. Whatever you have in the house will do for now.
The bail is set at twenty-two thousand, sir. It can be paid by bank transfer, or as a cash-in at any remittance counter, and I'll stay on the line with you the whole way so you're not doing it alone.

balks.prompt: "Twenty-two thousand." He says it slowly, and you hear the pencil stop. "That is my funeral money." A long moment. "Before I go anywhere, I am going to call his mother. You will wait, if you are who you say you are."

choices.text: Of course, sir. But she'll only be able to tell you what I already have, and every minute we're not on this he's still in that room. Let's get him out, and then we'll call her together.
Mr. Villanueva, if you hang up this line the bail window closes and I can't reopen it. Paolo asked for you. Not her.
Then call her, sir. I'll put a note on the file. Good afternoon.

paid.prompt: He reads the account number off a passbook he keeps in the hall drawer, one digit at a time, the way he would read it across a counter to a teller he trusted. Twenty-two thousand goes out against it: the funeral money, set aside so that nobody would have to pay for him. "Tell him," he says, before you can end the call. "Tell Paolo his Lolo says it is all right."
paid.consequence: He said Paolo's name before he said his own. After that I did not really hear anything else. I read the passbook number out to him the way I would read it to the bank, and I thanked him for staying on the line.

paid_part.prompt: "There is four thousand in the house. The rest is in the bank, and the bank is closed." He walks to the counter on the corner with the phone in his hand and you in his ear, and cashes in four thousand to a name he has never heard, and thanks the clerk, and thanks you.
paid_part.consequence: I sent what was in the house. Four thousand. I told the clerk it was for my grandson and she smiled at me. I think about her smiling at me.

refused.prompt: "No." Not loud. "I called my daughter on the other phone while you were talking, and Paolo is at school. He is sitting in a classroom." The pencil goes down. "I taught boys like you. I had hoped they grew out of it." He writes your number under the time and gives both to the police - the real ones.
refused.consequence: I called my daughter on the other phone while he was still talking. Paolo was in math class. It took four minutes to find that out, and he had told me there was no time.

hangs_up.prompt: "I don't believe you." It is not anger. It is worse than anger; it is disappointment, the particular kind a teacher keeps for a boy who could have done better. The line goes dead. He sits in the hall with the pencil for a while, and then he writes the number down, and then he calls his daughter to hear Paolo's voice.
hangs_up.consequence: I did not believe him, in the end. But I let him say my grandson's name three times before I stopped him, and I called my daughter afterward just to hear the boy breathing.

bail.prompt: "Hello? Attorney?" You are already gone. He sits by the phone for an hour in case it rings again, and then he calls his daughter, who tells him Paolo is fine, and then he does not sleep.
bail.consequence: A man said my grandson's name and then the line went dead. I called my daughter and he was at school. I have been waiting for them to call back and explain, and I know now that they never will.
